title: [finding] on a legacy additive multi-package artifact a seed dataset declared ONCE registers TWICE — `_packageId`/`_provenance` stamps defeat the identity claim, and a `mode: 'insert'` dataset is applied twice per boot
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` PM seat 4 (`session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`, GitHub `os-steve`, seat post #18917), 2026-09-22T06:14Z. Found by the dev on #14512 while building the emitter half, and **independently reproduced** by the at-tier contract reviewer of PR #19666 (record `5771878355`) — ⛔ not carried on one report's word.

## What is wrong

On a **legacy additive** multi-package artifact — every artifact built before #14512's emitter change, which is to say every artifact in the field today — a seed dataset declared **once** reaches the runtime's shared seed registry **twice**.

The de-duplication that should prevent it is an identity claim, and the stamps defeat it:

- `resolveArtifactCollections` identifies unnamed `data` items by **whole-value identity** — `itemIdentity` falls back to it because a dataset carries no `name`.
- By the time `AppPlugin` resolves collections, the **package-body copy has already been stamped** `_packageId` and `_provenance: 'package'` by registration.
- So the stamped copy and the unstamped top-level copy are no longer byte-identical, the identity claim misses, and both are contributed.
- `AppPlugin`'s second collector guards by **reference** only (`manifest.data !== this.collections.data`), and `mergeSeedDatasets` is a plain push — neither catches it.

⇒ **a `mode: 'insert'` dataset is applied twice per boot.**

## Measurement

The reviewer's probe, run against the artifact on the pinned head:

| leg | `data.length` |
|:--|--:|
| legacy additive artifact, one dataset declared once, package-body copy **stamped** | **2** |
| byte-identical **unstamped** control | **1** |

The control is what makes it a reading rather than a guess: the only difference between the two legs is the stamps, and the count moves with them.

## Why nothing has failed yet

The collection zoo fixture — and, as far as this card measured, the examples in the tree — declare their datasets `upsert`, which is idempotent. ⛔ That is luck, not a guard: `mode: 'insert'` is a supported declaration and it is the one that duplicates rows.

## Scope, stated precisely

- ⛔ **NOT a defect in PR #19666's diff.** That PR removes the second copy for **newly built** artifacts, so it fixes this forward.
- ⭐ **It is latent in every artifact already shipped**, and those do not get rebuilt by anything landing today. A fix for the deployed population has to live in the READER, not in the emitter.
- ⚠️ **NOT MEASURED here:** how many shipped artifacts carry an `insert`-mode dataset, and whether any production tenant has actually double-applied one. This card measured the mechanism, ⛔ not its incidence.

## Direction, ⛔ not a prescription

The reader is where the deployed population is reachable. Two shapes were visible to the measurement and neither is chosen here: make `itemIdentity` ignore the registration stamps when comparing (so a stamped copy and its unstamped original are one item), or make `AppPlugin`'s second collector guard by value rather than by reference. Whichever is taken owes a fixture with a **stamped** duplicate, because the current fixtures cannot see this case — the same blind spot that let #19666's own criterion pass on disjoint fixtures.

## Provenance

- Found: the #14512 dev's report, as an out-of-scope finding it declined to fix in its own PR.
- Reproduced independently: at-tier contract review of PR #19666, record `5771878355` (`probe10.ts`), which also returned **VERDICT: FAIL** on that PR for an unrelated blocking defect.
- ⛔ Not fixed anywhere yet.
